belief: “When my body reacts, the danger is happening now. I am not safe even here.”
belief_plain: When my body reacts, the danger is happening now. I am not safe even here
origins: The body remembers. A smell, a tone of voice, a posture, or a sudden sensation can bring a wave of fear, numbness, or the urge to flee, even when the room is safe. That reaction is not you being dramatic. The lie is the interpretation: “Because my body reacts, the danger is happening now, and I am not safe even here.” A counselor can help you tell a memory in the body from a threat in the room, without making you relive anything. A counselor can help you work with this at a pace that is safe. You do not have to do it alone, or all at once.
self: I have to get out or I will not survive this feeling.
If my heart is racing, I am in danger.
I am not safe in my own home, my church, or my car.
I should be over these reactions by now.
God is far away when I feel like this.
replacement: My body can react to a memory without the danger being here now. I can be startled and still be safe, and God is with me.
